rehearsal.title: What Does LitBuy Rehearsal Parcel Mean? Steps, Weight and Direct Shipping
rehearsal.description: Understand what a LitBuy rehearsal parcel means, when to use it instead of direct submission, and how to read packed weight and dimensions before paying.
sections: Rehearsal parcel means preparing and measuring selected warehouse goods before the final international shipping decision. It is a pre-shipping check of the proposed parcel, not a carrier tracking status or an automatic shipping discount. Check the account’s current service fee, processing range and whether payment or approval is required after the result.
A worked example and a packing instruction

Suppose selected goods weigh 4.0 kg after packing and the carton measures 40 × 30 × 25 cm. At an illustrative route divisor of 6,000, dimensional weight is 5.0 kg. If the route bills the higher of these weights, volume controls before its rounding rule. This is a hypothetical calculation, not a LitBuy route quote.
A useful instruction is: remove disposable outer cartons from soft clothing; keep protective support for the structured bag; do not compress its shape; photograph the final item list and measure the outer carton. Compare a smaller carton’s complete cost with the repacking fee and protection needs.
Rehearsal versus direct submission: choose by uncertainty

Use rehearsal when packed dimensions, mixed goods or packing changes could materially change the route or final cost. Direct submission may be reasonable for a compact, predictable parcel when the account’s estimate leaves enough budget margin. Both require QC acceptance and route eligibility checks. Neither guarantees cheaper freight. Verify whether any coupon supports the payment flow you select.

returns.title: LitBuy Warehouse Returns and Refunds: QC Evidence, Steps and Fees
returns.description: Handle a LitBuy warehouse return or exchange with SKU checks, QC evidence, seller eligibility and separate tracking for returned goods and refunds.
sections: A warehouse return is not yet a refund

A return request, seller approval, domestic return dispatch, seller receipt and refund credit are distinct events. Check them separately. A refund credited to an account balance is also different from money withdrawn to a payment method. Current seller terms and the account record determine eligibility, charges, destination and processing; this guide does not promise a fixed return window or free return.

Save the original product URL, order ID, paid price, selected SKU, arrival timestamp and the QC photo showing the precise issue. Explain the difference: for example, the order specifies one color while the warehouse label and photos show another. Request return eligibility before international parcel submission.
Record seller approval, return address supplied through the account, domestic return postage, service fees if displayed, expected refund basis and who pays each charge. Do not ship to an independently guessed address. Keep packing and seller-required accessories while the decision is pending.
Track the physical return and the money separately

Use one timeline for approval → dispatch → seller receipt, and another for requested amount → approved deduction → account credit → optional withdrawal. Save the domestic tracking number and refund transaction reference. If only one timeline has moved, ask support about the outstanding stage with its reference.
For illustration, if an eligible 100 CNY item refund has a separately agreed 12 CNY return expense, record the 100 CNY credit and 12 CNY expense independently; do not assume the platform always deducts that amount. This is a ledger example, not a current LitBuy fee.

weight.title: LitBuy Shipping Weight: Actual vs Volumetric Weight with Examples
weight.description: Calculate LitBuy parcel actual, volumetric and chargeable weight using worked dimension examples, route divisors and packing comparisons.
sections: Calculate from the packed outer carton

Volumetric weight (kg) = length × width × height in centimeters ÷ the route divisor. Where the selected route uses the higher of actual and volumetric weight, apply that comparison first, then its billing increment, minimum and rounding. Not every route uses the same rule. Read the current account quotation before paying.

Example A: 4.0 kg and 40 × 30 × 25 cm produce a volume of 30,000 cm³. At an illustrative divisor of 6,000, dimensional weight is 5.0 kg; at 5,000, it is 6.0 kg. Example B: 4.0 kg and 40 × 30 × 20 cm produce 24,000 cm³, or 4.0 kg at 6,000. These are arithmetic examples, not verified route settings or live prices.
On a route that bills the greater figure, Example A is controlled by volume while Example B reaches the actual-weight figure before rounding. Removing a few grams alone will not reduce Example A’s dimensional charge. Outer dimensions or the accepted billing rule must change.
Compare protection and total cost before repacking

A smaller carton may reduce a billing tier, but a repacking service can cost extra and fragile goods still need protection. Compare final freight plus requested packing services, rather than carton size alone. Recheck available routes after dimensions change. The calculator below estimates the unrounded comparison; it cannot calculate a live freight price or confirm eligibility.
